verdict.rationale: Blaxel documents several mechanisms that keep credentials away from sandboxed code. Its outbound proxy can inject secrets into headers and bodies, so credentials can be added at the network layer [blaxel-docs-27]. Workloads can run as an unprivileged user while the sandbox API keeps elevated privileges [blaxel-docs-30], per-domain allowlists and denylists block exfiltration [blaxel-docs-28], and frontend access uses scoped, time-limited session tokens [blaxel-docs-24]. However, no evidence explicitly states that secrets injected by the proxy, or the sandbox API's own credentials, cannot be read by the code running inside the sandbox; that guarantee is only implied. missing for 10: an explicit isolation guarantee (VM/kernel boundary) that host or platform credentials are unreachable from sandbox code, explicit confirmation that proxy-injected secrets never enter the sandbox, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
